When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training in 2010 when I stopped playing football to stay active and fit. I didn’t start training to fight, but my first coach told me he booked me a fight and if I didn’t take it I had to leave the gym…next thing I’m fighting and never looking back.

What ranks and titles have you held? I’ve held two Australian flyweight titles, one for Eternal MMA and one for Nitro MMA.I have a purple belt in BJJ

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? To fight in the UFC would be a dream come true, a goal I have strived to achieve for the last 10 years - the blood, the tears, all the hurdles and setbacks overcome with persistence and dedication and a will to never give up
It would mean everything to me to win a contract to fight in the UFC.

What was your job before you started fighting? I am a full-time mechanic, and I still currently work 40 hours a week on top of training camps to fight.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? I have won two Australian MMA titles, I have headlined all major shows in Australia, been the number 1 flyweight for four years, fought internationally on UAE Warriors, I have beat opponents from DWTCS and TUF  

Favorite grappling technique: Ground-and-pound

Favorite Striking technique: Flying knee

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started boxing at the age of 12 in order to stand my ground on the street. In Dagestan as a kid, I often had to fight, and my opponents could be gym-trained boys against whom you needed combat training. Just your natural abilities were not enough to resist them, and losing to someone was not my credo, so I went to the boxing gym.

What ranks and titles have you held? Master of Sports in Thai boxing and kickboxing, International Master of Sports in Burmese boxing, Master of Sport Candidate in combat sambo

Do you have any heroes? Pirate Hayreddin Barbarossa, Salahuddin Al Ayyubi and Imam Shamil.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It is a fulfillment of my dream and desire to become a champion.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Bachelor, specialty Business Analyst

What was your job before you started fighting? Student

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Winner of the International Boxing Tournament, International Muay Thai Tournament, All-Russian Muay Thai Competition, All-Russian Kickboxing Competition

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Champion of Eurasia in Burmese boxing, champion of the “Nashe Delo” organization, champion of the global MMA organization, champion of the TFC (Thailand fighting championship) organization, champion of the Bangla boxing stadium, champion of the Patong boxing stadium, winner of various international tournaments in China in MMA and K1, champion of Russia in Thai boxing among professionals.

Favorite grappling technique: Suplex

Favorite Striking technique: Backfist

When and why did you start training for fighting? My dad owns a martial arts gym (kickboxing). It’s a family business and I was put into it from a young age. Me and my sister, who is an Olympian in kickboxing, done it our whole lives. In 2017, my last year in kickboxing, me my dad and my sister were all on the national team together and competed in the world championship. My dad and sister both got bronze, and I got double gold in the point fighting and continuous fighting division. It was really special to share together. 

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Cage legacy 3 times, Multiple WAKO World title, Multiple WAKO European titles, IBBJF World title, IMMAF world title, World combat games champion

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines?  Kickboxing & TKD black belt, BJJ purple belt

Who is your favorite fighter and why?  My dad, MARTIN BANNON. LEGEND always look up to him. He fought till he was in his 50s at the highest level of kickboxing 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I’ve done leisure management and personal training straight after school, but then I went into finance. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked in Deloitte in finance. 

Personal Life/Background: Jayce Bannon, my son, who is 5 years old. He motivates me so f**king much. Having him as part of this journey is something I’ll forever be grateful for. Whenever times get tough and he’s sitting there making me laugh, it pushes me to go harder. I wanna be the best so I can give him the life he deserves. This comeback is personal. LET’S F**KING GO. Also, what’s up Dublin? Let’s get back!!!!

When and why did you start training for fighting? I've liked doing sports since childhood. First, I started with striking because, at the time, it was more popular in China due to kung fu films. Later, I started to learn wrestling, which really set me off on the path towards becoming a full-fledged MMA fighter. Wrestling is the most important part of MMA, so it was definitely an advantage to have early on when everybody else was strikers. 

What ranks and titles have you held? Level-2 Catch wrestler, Taekwondo black belt, Yunnan province kickboxing champion, Road to UFC season three strawweight winner

Do you have any heroes? In my story, I'm the hero.

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Before, I used to take this MMA / wrestling stuff very light-heartedly. Wrestling is physical chess, and it helps keep my mind sharp. It was just a fun hobby allowing me to relax and take my mind off my medical work. Even though I was winning MMA competitions on a regular basis, it was always secondary to my main job as a doctor. However, after being selected to join the UFC Performance Institute in Shanghai, I started treating it more seriously; sort of like a real job. It's definitely an exciting new chapter in my life.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I attended medical university in Kunming, and graduated as a licensed doctor. 

What was your job before you started fighting? Worked in a hospital as a licensed doctor. Also helping out our foreign residents with their companies in China.  

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? South-west Taekwondo champion, Yunnan province Kickboxing champion. Yunnan Traditional Wrestling tournament winner. 
Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Heroine FC champion

Favorite grappling technique: Top control

Favorite Striking technique: Punch to the face!

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training MMA in 2012. It’s been my dream since I was a kid, ever since I saw the UFC on TV. I couldn’t afford to train until I graduated and found the right opportunity, but once I got it, I ran with it.

Training: Three hours in the morning and four hours at night. This will be a mix of both striking and grappling class, sometimes substituted with a cardio session.

Do you have any heroes? My hero is my mother. She instilled my hardworking attitude and my sense of discipline.

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? To fight in the UFC means I’m where I belong. I’ve been saying I would be here since I was a child. It was only a matter of time.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to college for two semesters but left to chase my dreams.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was working at a pizza shop until my coach let me start working at his gym with the kids’ after school program.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I was 9-0 as an amateur, winning WKA, Cagezilla, and Spartyka titles.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: I’m a blue belt under Lloyd Irvin.

Favorite grappling technique: Kimura

Favorite Striking technique: Jab

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I started when I was 15 years old to lose weight, and because I come from a family of athletes.

What professional titles have you held? I’m the only professional MMA fighter from my state, Córdoba, Argentina.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Athlete of the Year from the Córdoba Confederation and amateur kickboxing champion

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? Blue Belt in BJJ

Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines? Brown Belt in Kickboxing

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? Anyela Pérez. I came out of the fight very injured, and had to change all my strategies.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Among women, for her style and precision, Valentina “The Bullet.” In every other way, I’m motivated by Esteban Ribovics, my teammate for many years and a standout Argentine fighter currently in the UFC.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My dad. He taught me how to be a true athlete and to always believe in myself.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I am a teacher (primary school teacher).

What was your job before you started fighting? I was a boxing and kickboxing teacher, I sold food, and worked as a waitress at schools.

Origin of nickname (The Witch): When I was doing kickboxing, during some sparring with teammates, I said that everyone was going to wake up with a spell on their heads.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? I want to help my family, give us the life we deserve, and open doors so more people from my country have the opportunity to step onto the UFC canvas.

Personal Life / Background (family stuff, kids, etc): From an athletic family (my dad was a professional soccer player). I had weight issues, suffered bullying, trained hockey and swimming, lived in a lower-middle-class neighborhood, and my dream is to take my family forward.

I don’t have a partner or children. I left my entire family, my pets, and all my loved ones in my country to live in Mexico and move forward. I like listening to music, spending time with friends, and learning new things. I like motorcycles, soccer, and cuarteto music.

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with (celebrities, content creators, other fighters, sports stars)? Bad Bunny, Messi and Jon Jones

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? Reading, listening to music, and riding motorcycles.
